text_fidelity_a: Gifts for Men Dad, Fathers Day, Husband Grandpa -Survival Kit Gear 16 in 1-Fishing Camping Hunting Hiking Gifts Ideas for Him-Cool Gadget Survival Gear We have been working on assembling a couple go bags for our family in case of an emergency, such as a natural disaster, fire, etc. WORSPODAY's 16-in-1 survival kit is the perfect addition to it. First of all, the price is on point and provides a huge savings over having to buy each of the items included individually. Second, we love the watertight hardback case that the tools come in. It has strong clasps on three sides and they don't just pop open. You have to tug pretty hard on them, so that actually is important so you don't lose your gear when you're on the move and may need it most. Second, the tactical gear that is included isn't cheaply made. These are durable products, such as the tactical pen (with a glass breaker on one end), flashlight (needs one AA battery), and the knife. Even the compass is fairly weighty in your hand and works very well. Also, because of the amount of detail that goes into these items, this whole kit makes a handsome gift that any outdoorsman would appreciate too. We also like the tactical bracelet because even if that is all you have on you, there is also a flint built in so you can start a fire, a whistle, and a compass. Also, it is made of paracord, so you can use it to tie up an emergency shelter or go fishing if need be. The manual that comes with it is detailed, but you will want to become well familiar with each item included and how to use it before you head out to the woods or on your trek as you may try to outrun a storm. Also, there are a few items included such as the glass breaker end of the pen, the saw, and of course the knife, which could cut someone, particularly a child, so you'll want to make sure those who handle it aren't going to accidentally injure themselves because these items are definitely not toys. All in all, however, this is an exceptional product, and I plan to recommend it to everyone I know who may be putting together their own go bag.
text_fidelity_b: Gifts for Men Dad, Fathers Day, Husband Grandpa -Survival Kit Gear 16 in 1-Fishing Camping Hunting Hiking Gifts Ideas for Him-Cool Gadget Survival Gear

I'm just able to get back to things and I think having this will aide my recovery - as per my doctor's instructions. Folding Stool with Storage Bag, Lightweight Outdoor Chair Aluminum Alloy Bracket Camping Stool for Fishing, Hiking, Camping, Traveling and BBQ (Silver) I”ll be honest, I did not get this Folding Stool with Storage Bag as a sitting stool but for my feet. We have a new chair from here on Amazon, that is a bit tall for my shorter legs and while the chair is comfortable, I knew that over longer periods of time it will start to be uncomfortable. I thought if I had a foot stool it would be better. Spotted this Folding Stool with Storage Bag and grabbed it. I was right - it goes perfectly with the chair. But it also will make a good additional sitting spot if needed. Or could hold some lighter things - well balanced if we’re careful. The Folding Stool with Storage Bag comes in that storage bag - pull it out and as you’re kind of moving it around, it starts to put itself into those legs. Meaning the legs go together very easily. They are like a lot of newer things - they are connected by a line that keeps them ‘together’ then push them into one another and they stay in place. I don’t know that I’m explaining it well, but it’s easy. Watch so the seat goes the correct way - if not, you’ll pull it open a little and flip it the right way - no worries. And you’re good. I’m a heavier guy right now. I sat on it, but didn’t really put my full weight on it - and for me it was only sort of comfortable at this weight. My wife is lighter, but she too was so-so on sitting comfort. I think a smaller person or child would do best. It was fairly sturdy for the weight - but I would not last too long on it and she didn’t think she would either. But using it to prop my legs across was just fine. Felt good, was comfortable, and I am pretty sure it’ll be great for that kind of thing.

In the end I gave it 4 rather than 5 stars because of the ability to hold a larger person is not there, and even at a smaller weight, I don’t think it’s wide enough for someone to go very long on. I have not always been my current weight and it is coming off, but even when I get back down, I don’t think it would be comfortable enough to last more than a few minutes without preferring to move to a chair. But, for a foot rest, it’s good. I am glad to have this Folding Stool with Storage Bag, but it will “only” work for limited things.
text_fidelity_b: Folding Stool with Storage Bag, Lightweight Outdoor Chair Aluminum Alloy Bracket Camping Stool for Fishing, Hiking, Camping, Traveling and BBQ (Silver)

SABRE Runner Pepper Gel, Maximum Police Strength OC Spray, Reflective Hand Strap for Easy Carry & Quick Access, 35 Bursts, Secure & Easy to Use Safety, Optional Clip-On Alarm & LED Armband Combos I have always kept pepper spray in both my car and home for safety reasons, and even in my purse. There are times when the only thing you have to protect yourself may be just pepper spray. Whether it's an animal or person meaning to do you harm, having pepper spray may be the only thing that gives you that precious moment to get away and stay safe. Living in a Cleveland suburb, I have had close calls and pepper spray is a must for even our postmen, as you never know if those unleashed dogs are red zone or not.

The first time I found I needed any type of protection was when I was taking flowers to our family's cemetery in Cleveland. There were actually people in hoodies stalking us- I was not alone- to the point where my husband took his golf club out of the car and held it like a baseball bat. Just having the pepper spray attached to my arm is a huge relief. I don't have to get it out of the glove compartment or my purse- which I never carry when I'm walking or doing things anyway. For walkers or bike riders, this convenient arm band is a must for protection. If only the 3 teenagers abducted by Ariel Castro in Cleveland had pepper spray, what a different outcome that could have been.

Sabre Red made a Pepper Gel Spray in an earlier model of this armband type, which had a wider and unbelievably uncomfortable armband, and it never stayed on your arm. They redesigned the armband on this new model- it stays on your arm, it's very narrow (1 1/2 inches wide) and it doesn't hurt like the wide one. Just know that it is made of velcro- so it won't feel like a soft piece of cotton (the underside is comfortable enough though), but being narrow, I like that there is less velcro on your arm. I like the buckle on the band, to keep the end from sticking out also. You can make it as tight as you like and I have no slipping or discomfort at all. At 20 inches long, this band will fit all arm sizes- even those larger biceps.

The canister of the red pepper gel spray has an ON/OFF position for your safety. The tight elastic sleeve has the velcro strip all the way down the side of the canister, so you can attach it to the arm band anywhere. There is also a strip of reflective tape on the side for additional safety from vehicles if you are walking or bike riding at night. My sister is a bike rider and she had to use this pepper gel on an attacking dog. She sprayed the dog in the eyes and it kept running along side her bike trying to grab her leg. She said she sprayed it again hitting it in the nose and mouth- that slowed it down and the dog finally turned around. So, I guess with a dog, that sense of smell just keeps on going until it gets sprayed in the nose.

As for the gel spray itself, it goes the full 12 feet when sprayed. You will get some fine mist coming back at you when the wind is against you, so protect your face. Make sure you test the spray first, so you know how far the spray will reach and to make certain you have a good canister. Sabre Gel has made great improvements on both the armband and gel spray on this Pepper Gel Duathlete Arm Band. The arm band is nice and narrow, comfortable and stays put. The Pepper Gel has just a little mist spray back, so you still need to protect your own face. It's a great 5 Star Improved Pepper Gel Spray and Armband, that hopefully you will not have to use, but if you need to use it, it can truly be a life saver.
text_fidelity_b: SABRE Runner Pepper Gel, Maximum Police Strength OC Spray, Reflective Hand Strap for Easy Carry & Quick Access, 35 Bursts, Secure & Easy to Use Safety, Optional Clip-On Alarm & LED Armband Combos

text_fidelity_a:
Apurioni Kayak Seat with Back Support Adjustable Straps and Deluxe Padded Cushion with Waterproof Storage Bag My wife and I love the water and have taken a number of SUP or Kayak tours over the years, so we decided to get our own SUPs so we can get out when we want. We are very happy with this Apurioni Kayak Seat with Back Support Adjustable Straps and Deluxe Padded Cushion.

I’ve recently been able to get a couple inflatable SUPs and we can’t wait to get to use them (NOTE: in our state flotation devices are required and we have not been able to get those yet. Therefore, we have not yet been on the water to use these. We are also beginners at doing and owning these, so please consider this when reading). I’ve always preferred kayaking over SUPing, mainly because having spent my life into my 30s playing sports, the ankles have taken a number of hits and at this point, can get sore quickly - SUPing involves a lot of wear and tear on the ankles. So I have looked at inflatable kayaks, not finding anything I think is of a quality that matches inflatable SUPs. And to that end, my wife and I have gotten inflatable SUPs instead. But, I also knew that I could use the inflatable SUP as a kayak on its own, but if I added this Apurioni Kayak Seat with Back Support Adjustable Straps and Deluxe Padded Cushion it would give me some of the same support as a kayak seat. In the end, I am very glad I grabbed this Apurioni Kayak Seat. This is actually the second of two such seats, so both of us can use a seat on our SUP. This Apurioni Kayak Seat seems to be well designed, with good, solid construction, and good materials. There were no instructions and we’d not used such things before, so it came to common sense to put together and that was easy enough. The seat attaches by 4 hooks to the SUP’s D Rings on the surface. You adjust the tension of the straps to make sure it’s secure and at a good position, and in doing so, once seated, it holds the seat in place. Both of us tried this Apurioni Kayak Seat and found it comfortable. It is not meant to be the same kind of chair you sit on in your living room, but we both found this gives one support to help “support” sitting for a longer period of time. We have not taken it out, so I don’t know the longevity - I’ll come back and update if I have any issues once we can get out there - but for now, it seems like it’ll be a great support on a SUP trip. The material also seems like it’ll hold up fine to salt water, but we plan to wash it every use with fresh water post-use. There is a detachable bag on the bag, connected by clips, allowing you to carry things with (like water - tight bag for your gear - that would go inside this non-water proof bag, and can be detached so you can carry it separately. In the end, this seems like it’s going to be a good seat for our needs and we can’t wait to get out there and use it!
text_fidelity_b: Apurioni Kayak Seat with Back Support Adjustable Straps and Deluxe Padded Cushion with Waterproof Storage Bag

text_fidelity_a:
TETON Sports Camping Cot with Patented Pivot Arm - Folding Camping Cot for Car & Tent Camping - Durable Canvas Sleeping Cot - Portable Camping Accessory - 86" x 45" - Outfitter XXL I used this XXL cot for 30 days straight and had little issues with it. 5'10" & 240lbs. Being on the shorter side I could not swing my legs out of bed in the morning and easily reach the ground while still seated on the fabric portion. Being mindful of that if you do have to briefly sit on the edge of the frame aim for the center point, it's the strongest. Sitting cross-legged in fabric sections while reading or watching movies did not feel uncomfortable at all.
If you are a dedicated back sleeper you could use it as is without padding if you had to. Side sleepers might want some padding, I found even a 1/4" went a long way. However, I am looking in to a camping pad for the next excursion.
No matter the cot the fabric will stretch with prolonged use, so don't be surprised that there is more slack after a couple of days then when you started. Sag was minimal after 30 days of use and I didn't feel it affected my comfort level at all.
I wanted a sheet to give me a barrier between the rough textured padding I used and my skin and my biggest issue was keeping it from bunching up in the cot thru the night. If you go this route I would suggest trying a drawstring sheet. If using blankets for top cover go Full size or bigger. The added fabric drapes and helps form a seal to keep out cold air.
Still more comfortable than my aged spring mattress, and after going back to my real bed I am now rethinking having put the cot away...
text_fidelity_b: TETON Sports Camping Cot with Patented Pivot Arm - Folding Camping Cot for Car & Tent Camping - Durable Canvas Sleeping Cot - Portable Camping Accessory - 86" x 45" - Outfitter XXL

Sougayilang Chest Waders for Men and Women with Boots, Waterproof Hunting Waders with Phone Waterproof Pouch or Boot Hanger-size 12 For what they are, they actually do pretty well. I bought them for my semi-annual trout trip. Keep in mind, folks, definitely NOT lined, so if you’re looking for a warm pair, keep looking. If you’re not a wimp and don’t mind a few layers underneath, then these aren’t bad.

My only issue is that I discovered a few leaks in them near the boots after my first couple of hours using them. It lead me to believe they probably had this problem right out of the packaging. Now, in the grand scheme, I only trout fish a couple times a year, and for how miniscule the leaks were, I sucked it up and just used them for the 2.5 days I needed them. Never got so bad that water was pooling up inside of them, but enough to soak my leg from the top of the boot down. I’d guess that it was coming in at the seam where the leg and boot met. Definitely could have been worse, but that was still a big inconvenience for me. I’m not sure how to contact the seller, because I’d like to possibly get a replacement pair. I’m hoping they see this review and can contact me.

All in all, aside from that leaking issue, the next couple days they held up against me kneeling on rocks/logs to retie and they were pretty comfy after wearing them for several hours. I’d recommend taking them somewhere for 30 mins to an hour and wearing them in water before taking them on a 4 hour trip like me and getting surprised. 4/5 stars due to the small leaks. If the seller holds true to the other reviews I’ve seen, and can make it right, I’d say these are 5/5 stars for sure. For $50 or less you can have a decent pair of unlined waders, can’t beat that anywhere else.

text_fidelity_a:
SHIMANO CS-6500 Ultegra Bicycle Cassette (9-Speed) I'm an intermediate level cyclist who recently moved to the Denver area. After nearly dying on a 2800 foot climb over 15 miles I noticed my riding buddy had about a gear and a half lower than me. I looked around and finally swapped my stock Ultegra 12/23 to this 12/27 on my 1998 Specialized Allez Sport with a triple crank (52-42-30).

After pricing the extra tools I needed to do a swap, it wasn't much more $ to just hand this cassette and a new chain to my local bike shop and have them do the work - still saved $50-$60 using my own parts. Since I have a triple, I also have a long derailleur, so besides the chain, there's nothing more needed for the swap except for adjusting the derailleur for the bigger sprocket. I think 27 is as big as I can go, BTW, given the range of teeth on my crank.

I haven't been back to that hill yet, but this cassette and new chain are doing fine so far. My second gear (running middle ring) is now like my first gear was. Given the 12T top end, I didn't give up any high gearing, but I do need to get used to the bigger jump between 5th and 6th gear (I think that's the spot).

My riding buddy has a double with an 11-speed cassette. I think we're pretty close on highest and lowest ratios now. Sorry, I don't recall what he's got. But its a fairly high end bike with 11x2.
text_fidelity_b: SHIMANO CS-6500 Ultegra Bicycle Cassette (9-Speed)

text_fidelity_a:
Splatterburst Targets - 12 x12 inch (5) Bullseye Reactive Shooting Target - Shots Burst Bright Fluorescent Yellow Upon Impact - Gun - Rifle - Pistol - Airsoft - BB Gun - Air Rifle I use these splatter targets whenever I have to sight in a new .22 rifle. Each rifle I buy has a threaded barrel so that I can attach an AAC suppressor and do the shooting in my backyard. Using a 4X scope or higher allows you to easily keep track of your hits without having to rely on another person or a spotting scope. Since no one has a clue as to what I'm doing, I can take the time to do a good job with each rig.

First off I use a boresighter on the larger center target to zero each gun in properly. When I'm satisfied with my efforts, I'll then use three bullets from a different manufacturer--or a different configuration from the same manufacturer--on each of the four smaller targets to determine which ammo each gun likes best. I usually have about eight different types of ammo on hand so it takes two of these splatter targets to get the job done.

When I put each gun back in the rack, I tape the bottom of each stock with the name of the ammo that seems to work best in that gun/scope combination. After a few days I'll take the newly sighted in guns back outside to try the different types of ammo once more--just to be sure. Since I'm able to do this in my own backyard it saves me a lot of time driving to/from the range and waiting out the other shooters to change targets. I've also used this method to break in some suppressed .22 pistols.

Great targets, easy to use and easy to see.
text_fidelity_b: Splatterburst Targets - 12 x12 inch (5) Bullseye Reactive Shooting Target - Shots Burst Bright Fluorescent Yellow Upon Impact - Gun - Rifle - Pistol - Airsoft - BB Gun - Air Rifle

text_fidelity_a:
Timex T5J031 Unisex Digital Fitness Heart Rate Monitor Watch I ask one thing of this watch, and it delivers: count my pulse. What I did not expect is that it would be as accurate as it is. I compared to various treadmills I run on, including [[ASIN:B0010XI81E Life Fitness Club Series Treadmill]] and found the watch more accurate than the handlebar pulse monitors.

* The chest straps fits well enough for me.
* Modes are easy to switch.
* The watch fits fine, but can be a little difficult to take off.
* My average heart rate worked well.
* Easy to use lap function. As mostly a neighborhood street and dedicate running/biking path runner, I use this when I cross the street.
* The Indiglo light is difficult to see - not especially bright, and the button for it is in a difficult to reach spot while running (top left as opposed to front). After a few miles, when I just a quick look, it can be a nuisance while running through a shady area. In fact, while lit, unless in a pitch black environment, the numbers are actually more difficult to see.
* The description says, "The Night Mode feature allows you to illuminate the Indiglo night-light for 3 seconds with any button press, regardless of the mode or function." I was unable to get this to work with any other button.

For the price, I would like to see better engineering. While I understand this is an entry level pulse monitor, set-up is an unnecessary challenge.

Anthony Trendl
[...]
text_fidelity_b: Timex T5J031 Unisex Digital Fitness Heart Rate Monitor Watch

text_fidelity_a:
Gelindo Tactical Backpack with Bladder - Insulated Military Pack with Molle System I bought this for my fiancé for Christmas, he needed a new emergency backpack. You never really know what you’re getting when you’re ordering stuff like this online...one review will say it’s garbage, the next will say it’s the best thing ever. I’m pretty good at judging which ones are accurate, and which ones are super-biased - either for or against.

This is a very good backpack! It’s worth more than what they’re charging for it. I looked (in person) at some 3.11 Tactical backpacks, and, this measures up in every single aspect, at a fraction of the price (for those that haven’t seen them, they’re generally well over $100). Also, the 3.11s that I looked at didn’t have padded waist straps like this one, and didn’t come with the bladder, like this one does. The padded waist straps alone up the value, plus there’s small zipper pockets on them to stash keys or whatever in...they don’t hold a plus size iPhone though. Just a smidge too small. You don’t realize how important padded waist straps can be until you’re stuck with carrying 30lbs on your back and those plain straps are digging into you, even through a heavier coat.

The padding in the back is just as good as the Swiss Army backpack I have, it’s not itchy if it gets against your skin, and it does pretty good at keeping you cool...as cool as you can be with a bag strapped to your back, at least.

There’s plenty of pockets so you can organize you’re supplies for better accessibility and it does have the nice straps on the bottom to attach a bedroll (yoga mat, if you choose) or pup tent. There’s plenty of places to add/attach other accessories and pouches. Also, the compartment for the bladder is insulated. I can’t really say how well because we haven’t tested it, but it seems it would be decent.

All around, this is just a really, really good pack, especially for the price! I fully intend on buying myself one very soon because all of my backpacks are shot (my “everyday”, and my emergency bags), and this just fit the bill...I almost kept it for myself! 😁
text_fidelity_b: Gelindo Tactical Backpack with Bladder - Insulated Military Pack with Molle System

My area is abutted by Army Corp of Engineer "wild" land that goes (about a quarter of a mile) to a large lake not far from my house.  Just this past week my neighbor and I spotted a bobcat in the wild land back there!  We have coyotes, wild boars, raccoons, opossums, armadillos and a few other critters we've seen and documented.  This laser range finder has allowed me to get an idea of how close some of the wild life is getting to my yard.  I have small dogs and the coyotes worry me more than most of the other critters.  So when I spot one slinking around the edge of the woods, I grab this range finder and document when, where and how far they were from me.  At some point, if they get to be a bit too bold, the neighbors and I will have to report the pack as being dangerous.  Having documented the times, the places and how far they were from me, a human, will be helpful in proving that they need to be trapped and moved or dealt with in some other way.  I know this range finder is good for golf or even hunting - I guess my use is more akin to hunting, but I will say that it is easy to use, sighting in on the critter to find the distance.  That's what I need to know!

text_fidelity_a:
Wahoo Blue SC Speed and Cadence Sensor for iPhone, Android and Bike Computers I have been using the Digifit iPhone app for several months now and the first speed/cadence sensor I got for my bike was the [[ASIN:B000BFNOT8 Garmin GSC 10 Speed/Cadence Bike Sensor]]. that worked great except the magnets on the crank arm/pedal were troublesome. I did, however get some strong ("rare earth") little magnets and stuck those on the end of my pedal and that worked like a charm. The thing about the Garmin GSC10 is that it uses the ANT+ technology. It worked okay with my iPhone 3GS, but the battery life on that old phone didn't always last through my 2+ hour rides. So, I upgraded to the iPhone 5 and now I'm able to take advantage of the Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE or Bluetooth 4.0) technology.

I got this Wahoo speed and cadence sensor that uses the BLE technology to connect to my iPhone 5 and send the data to the DigiFit app that I use. The device attaches just fine to my road bike. I was able to connect it with the thick rubber band provided, but I was weary that it would pop off during my long rides, so I used the zip-ties instead. The magnets that I needed/used with the Garmin were replaced with the ingenious little magnet band that slips easily onto the pedal crank arm. Wahoo got that figured out nicely!

The other thing I like about this device over the Garmin GSC10 is the use of the Bluetooth. Granted, you need a device that uses it, but I notice that my iPhone 5 gets connects to the sensor much quicker and stays connected better than the Garmin did. When I stop for a period of time on my bike rides I usually pause the DigiFit app. With the Garmin and iPhone 3GS using the ANT+ technology it often wouldn't find the device right away and I'd have to retry the connection to get going. I haven't had that issue at all with this Wahoo. Granted, this could be a function of the iPhone, the ANT+ or the Garmin - any combination of those could have caused the issue.

I can't speak to how it works with the Wahoo app, since, as mentioned, I only have used it with the DigiFit app on both the iPhone 3Gs and the iPhone 5. But I really like this sensor and would definitely recommend it.
text_fidelity_b: Wahoo Blue SC Speed and Cadence Sensor for iPhone, Android and Bike Computers

Planet Bike Sport Spot 4 LED Bicycle Light with Head, and Handlebar Mounts This is a great light for riding in cities. It's very bright for being seen by drivers and pedestrians and even for maneuvering though some rough patches of asphalt on dimly lit streets. While there are four modes, the only ones to use are all lit or all blinking (I don't see the point of having just the two outer or inner LEDs on). The battery life is also fairly long, but definitely not 100 hours as claimed, even on blinking mode.

I've used this light while riding through moderate rainfall and it has worked perfectly. The handlebar mount is very stable and it's easy to release the light when locking up (yet it has never fallen off due to bumps). The small size is another benefit when carrying it in your jacket pocket.

I've used the light as a headlamp while camping and don't like it much for that. The headband is very uncomfortable since there's no cushion on the mounting bracket. I'm left with a sore indentation on my forehead. The light also does not tilt like a good headlamp should.

I will say that I disagree with the description calling it a "larger" size sleep mask. It definitely is not that.  When I got the package in the mail, I opened the mask and thought this is way too small for me. BUT, I soon realized that while average in size, this sleep mask is really amazing!  First, it isn't the typical fabric (satin) that you find in masks.  It is a sort of microfiber fabric. It really helps the mask stay in place while sleeping. It isn't fancy as far as the way you put it on. It is the same velcro you find in nearly all masks. I remedy this by sewing a tube of fabric around the velcro part because I don't like it pulling my hair.  I was amazed at how well this small mask really does block out the light.  I am almost ready to say that it blocks out light better than any of the dozens of masks I have purchased over the years.  All in all, I am super happy with my purchased and I would recommend it!

text_fidelity_a:
Bike Hoist Bicycle Lift for Garage Ceiling Storage, Heavy Duty Mountain Bicycle Hanging Rack with 3 Pulley and 45 ft Adjustable Rope | 100 lb Capacity You could assemble the components for a better bike hoisting system at any decent hardware store, but the part you would buy would cost two or three times as much, and you would spend a fair amount of time figuring out what to buy and how to assemble it.

I see several review that report the packaging indicates a lesser weight capacity than the 100 lb indicated in the listing. My packaging shows the weight capacity as 45 kg -- 100 lb. Regardless, I am confident that, in fact, much more than 100 lb. could be supported by this hardware. The actual limiting factor on weight capacity will not be the hardware provided, but rather the installation method. The box includes screws with plastic anchors that are normally used for installing screws in sheetrock. Anyone who uses those to attach to a sheetrock ceiling will almost certainly have a problem. Even if the plastic anchors are used to attach the hardware to wood trusses the result will be weaker than if screwed directly into the wood after a proper size hole has been pre-drilled. Other reviews contain suggestions for mounting. The instructions provided fail to provide guidance on the need for a secure mounting.

It is easy to overlook on the installation instructions the correct routing of the rope used for lifting. There is a hole in the cam lock fitting through which the cord should be threaded. Unfortunately the hole is barely large enough for the provided rope, which would make it difficult to upsize the rope.

Which brings me to the issue of the gaps between pulley cheeks and the sheaves. The gap is enough that the provided rope can jump out of the sheave groove and become wedged. The sheaves are designed so that squeezing the cheeks to reduce the gap results in friction at the axle before the gap is significantly reduced. While a larger rope could eliminate the risk of jamming, the hole in the cam lock does not permit such a substitution. It is for this reason, and the potential that a person could be misled by the plastic sheetrock anchors and fail to attach to solid wood, that I am giving 4 stars rather than 5.

Additional comments -- As others mention, the hooks to hang the bike do not really have enough curve to hold securely and you probably will need to do some bending to get a good result. My seat does not have a structure to which the hooks would attach, so I use a cord under a frame section and secure the hooks to that. If you have a speedometer or the like mounted on handle bars there is a possibility of conflict with hooks, and you may need to be careful to avoid damage to any wire connecting to a sensor. The cleat provided to tie off the rope when the bike is lifted is definitely pretty cheesy, but the cam lock is good enough that the cleat is really not needed. If you are a belt and suspenders person you might want to upgrade the cleat. Otherwise the cleat basically just provides a method to get excess rope out of the way.

So while this is not perfect, it provides a good solution at a good price, and I would buy another one if I had a second bike.
text_fidelity_b: Bike Hoist Bicycle Lift for Garage Ceiling Storage, Heavy Duty Mountain Bicycle Hanging Rack with 3 Pulley and 45 ft Adjustable Rope | 100 lb Capacity

text_fidelity_a:
Mirrycle MTB Bar End Mountain Bicycle Mirror , Black First, I had used these for decades. If the bike falls on the left side, any mirror is likely to break but I would always replace a broken mirror with this model.

There is a thin brass threaded barrel inside the base. That threaded barrel is there to accept the screw. Twice now, on two different mirrors purchased a week apart, that threaded barrel has come out of the base. In theory it could be glued back into the base but the barrel is so thin that it breaks at the slightest pressure of a pliers needed to get the barrel off of the screw, so that it might be glued back into the base. It really should be glued at the factory but recently it seems it is not.

By the way, the manufacturer sells replacement parts but asks $4 to ship what could be shipped for the price of two postal stamps. In my case it would cost $10 yet you can buy the entire mirror for $12 so what's the point of offering parts?

Update: I grew tired of replacing plastic mirrors every time the bike falls on the side with the mirror so I opted to get a metal motorcycle mirror here: [[ASIN:B005DSPO82 UNIVERSAL BAR END HANDLEBAR MOUNT MIRROR BLACK 6212041]]. I believe mountain bike handlebars are the same inside dimension as a 7/8 inch motorcycle handlebar (1 inch outside diameter) so most any motorcycle mirror should fit, especially the ones that mount in the bar end as this mirror does.
text_fidelity_b: Mirrycle MTB Bar End Mountain Bicycle Mirror , Black

Merrithew at Home SPX Reformer Bundle There are several issues here to consider prior to purchasing.

1. Will the carriage roll smoothly? Even after cleaning the rails, my stott SPX failed to roll smoothly. This is a really important point.

2. Are the hand/foot loops large enough to accommodate normal sized, adult hands and feet? My stott SPX came with super tiny hand/feet loops that wouldn't work for a six year old, let alone an adult. And I have very small, adult hands.

3. Is the carriage padding sufficient? My stott SPX arrived with very thin padding and it hurt the back during movements.

4. Is this the best price on the market? Absolutely not. This package sells elsewhere on the internet for up to $500 less with additional dvd's included.

5. Will stott respond to inquiries? My phone calls and emails were ignored. It's as if this company only responds to large commercial accounts. You're completely on your own and out of luck if there is a problem or if you have a question.

6. Is the delivery box manageable? My stott SPX came in one box, approximately 14 feet long. Inside this massive box there were a couple smaller boxes. But you're talking something akin to tremendous problems getting it from curbside into the house, and if like me, you return it for being an incredible waste of money and a huge disappointment, it is painful to deal with a 14 foot box that won't fit into any normal car or suv. Hope you have a truck handy.

7. Check out other reformer brands. For a little more money the quality soars. You might think cheap is ok now, but you won't use a poor quality reformer in the long run.
text_fidelity_b: Merrithew at Home SPX Reformer Bundle

text_fidelity_a:
StoreYourBoard Replacement 12 Inch Balloon Wheels Kayak Dolly and Sand Carts, Big Beach Buggy Inflatable Tires We loved the Rio Wonder Wheeler concept, but it didn't work so great in practice. When loaded, it was very difficult to pull over the sand. We then looked at higher-priced ones with balloon wheels, knowing that those would work better on soft sand. I convinced my husband to try these wheels on the Wonder Wheeler first. We followed the advice of other reviewers and bought a 36" length - 3/8" diameter steel rod from ACE (couldn't find one at Home Depot) and 4 metal flat washers to fit the rod (which would be used as new axle). We drilled a hole 1/2 inch from both ends using a titanium drill bit (the carbide one we bought was useless). We used 1/2" pvc pipe cut to the width of the new wheels. We inflated the tires to 4 lbs. with an electric pump; removed linch pins from original axle (don't lose these or plastic bushings), removed original big plastic wheels, bushings, and axle.
To assemble with new tires: 1) We inserted new axle; 2) then the original bushings (with end protrusion cut off); 3) then a metal washer; 4) new tire with pvc inserted through center; 5) another washer; and 6) inserted original linch pins through drilled holes (repeat steps 2-6 on other side). It now works like a dream and saved us several hundred dollars since we didn't have to buy a new cart.
text_fidelity_b: StoreYourBoard Replacement 12 Inch Balloon Wheels Kayak Dolly and Sand Carts, Big Beach Buggy Inflatable Tires

Kip leather is usually the most preferred leather among professional players due to the light, firm, feel and higher quality of the leather. Kip leather comes from younger cattle, which creates a lighter hide that is extremely durable and taut, while also being a little bit easier to break in when compared to USA premium steerhide gloves.

Selecting Your Leather:

Cowhide Leather - Heavy leather, fastest break in time, medium quality, short durability, ideal for youth players.

Steerhide Leather - Heaviest leather, longest break in time, high quality, longest durability, ideal for high school and college players.

Kip Leather - Lighter leather, medium break in time, higher quality, long durability, ideal for college and pro players.

Japanese Kip Leather - Lightest leather, medium break in time, highest quality, long durability, ideal for elite pro players.

Texsport Portable Outdoor Camping Shower Privacy Shelter Changing Room, Gray, 1 Count (Pack of 1) Most of the state parks here in CA have their showers turned off due to the drought, or want you to pay $2 for a 2 minute shower. This item makes for a great changing room for those that have smaller tents and can't stand up. The floor liner is VERY slippery once wet. Keep your sandals on when showering. It's also very important to place on as level a surface as possible. Due to our campsite configuration we couldn't get a perfect spot so I found myself fighting a little bit to not slip. You can easily get two normal length showers out of one bag. The bags are VERY heavy when completely filled. If you aren't that tall you may need some help hanging the bag.

Pros: Light, easy to set up, price
Cons: Once the shower bag is mounted, the end of the nozzle was already down to my chest. Get used to squatting, holding one hand on the nozzle and the other hand lathering or rinsing yourself. This can get very hard if you have long hair you are trying to shampoo.

Suggestions:
1. Make a more horizontal shower bag so that it doesn't hang so low.
2. A towel rack inside would be nice. In all honestly, there isn't enough water flow to get anything else wet. I used the mesh toiletry bags for my dry clothes.

text_fidelity_a:
H2OSUP Inflatable Stand Up Paddle Board 10'6''/10' × 30" × 6" with Premium SUP Paddle Board Accessories & Backpack, Ultra-Light, Wide Stable Design, Non-Slip Deck for Youth & Adults My wife and I have wanted to get on the water with SUPs or kayaks since trying them on a tour a few years ago, however, unable to have any storage at home, we have been unable to. Then we saw inflatable SUPs and thought we’d be able to give that a try. I had the opportunity to get this H2OSUP Inflatable Stand Up Paddle Board and I jumped! Of course, we live in a hot weather state with summer rainy (storm) season and I’ve had major surgery this year with a longer recovery, so unfortunately we have not yet been able to get onto the water. But as the weather calms and I’ve been cleared... we’ll be out there sooner than later. In the mean time, we finally had a chance to blow up this H2OSUP Inflatable Stand Up Paddle Board and so far so good - we are sure this is going to turn out to be a great thing for us! This H2OSUP Inflatable Stand Up Paddle Board comes with several items to get you going (able cuff, repair kit, pump), but do not forget, you’ll want to have some sort of safety vest (required by law in our state - NOT INCLUDED in this kit).

The pump to get it inflated is included and for us, worked pretty well. We took turns to pump it up and while it took some time (and strength we’re both currently lacking post surgery and injury) we were still able to get it “almost fully inflated.” I say “almost” because the company recommended 15 PSI and we only got to 10. That 15 is for “optimal use” and no higher. We felt like the 10 would be good, but when we are out there (and I have more energy back) we will go a bit higher than the 10 As you can see in the pics, it is very inflated and looks good, my wife able too and on it and feel firm and secure. Standing on it she said it felt like (on water) it’ll have good, solid balance and allow a feeling of security on the water. This SUP looks and feels “narrow and long” to us based on our experiences on tours, but something we both would feel comfortable on. We will update this review once we can get out there. In the mean time, we are really happy with this SUP and how easily it went together. Or blown into shape. The removal of air was easy and took only a couple minutes. I’ll say, when she first opened the valve there was a LOUD HIGH PITCHED!!! sound that hurt both our ears, but it went away pretty quickly. Then completed the air removal. My wife did point out the ONE CON is this H2OSUP Inflatable Stand Up Paddle Board has a VERY pointy and painful value piece you push on - it was not at all comfortable and hurt her finger enough she grabbed a piece of the wrapping it came in to cushion her finger.

We have not used nor opened the paddle that came with. We felt like its weight in the bag was alright, but had a chance to get another that was lighter. We will try both. But we also feel like having two paddles is safest - one with in case something happens to the second.

There are hooks on the deck where you can attach a kayak seat for sitting down - something I prefer. I have weaker ankles from years of sports, so I can tire easily on SUPs. I’ll look forward to this addition - NOT INCLUDED in this kit, but available from H2O as an add-on.

Overall this H2OSUP Inflatable Stand Up Paddle Board is a great board and we are even more excited to get to our coast and use it. In the mean time, we are very happy with how easy this SUP gets set up and takes down and feel like it’s sturdy and well made enough it’ll be great for a good long time.
text_fidelity_b: H2OSUP Inflatable Stand Up Paddle Board 10'6''/10' × 30" × 6" with Premium SUP Paddle Board Accessories & Backpack, Ultra-Light, Wide Stable Design, Non-Slip Deck for Youth & Adults

SOG Throwing Knives with Sheath 3 Pack Balanced Throwing Knives Set w/ Paracord Knife Handles and Professional Throwing Knife Sheath (F041TN-CP) I'm a knife/hatchet/weapon collector with probably over 400 blades in my collection. My first strong impression is always from seeing the blade, some just jump out at me from a visually striking perspective. In my experience, if they look good in a picture, they'll feel good in my hand. Very few times have I been disappointed in a blade purchase--if so, I just give it away--but I've learned to trust my instincts. I'm not talking about the weird fantasy stuff you see out there, I collect practicable and usable blades both old and new, some inexpensive but a good value, and some unbelievably expensive and worth it only for the investment value.

First off, I own three SOG products: a large Creed knife, an SOG Access Card, and a Tactical Tomahawk. All represent good value for the money and are well-constructed for their purpose. So it was a no-brainer for me to order the SOG Throwing Knives. But wait, these are more than throwing knives. Let me point out a few positives:

1. They are well designed, made of relatively thick steel, have a long cutting edge, and are well balanced.
2. The long cutting edge makes them much more than only a thrower, the grip is comfortable and the choils help prevent your hand from slipping forward to the blade.
3. They can be comfortably and effectively handled with stabbing, slashing, and back handed grips.
4. They will obviously handle any cutting chores assigned to them--once you sharpen the blades properly.
5. If not used to make tent pegs, they are long enough to be used as tent pegs in a pinch.
6. The paracord on the handles could be unwrapped and used for a multiple of purposes in the field.

And of course there are some negatives, but they aren't deal breakers considering the price:

1. Mine did not come sharp. That is easily rectified with a proper sharpening and can quickly be brought to the desired edge.
2. The sheath, while of a practical design, is not strongly made and I would expect it to not hold up long under constant use.
3. Although well balanced, I prefer throwing knives that are double edged at the tip and that are also longer and with more weight. At my size these feel insubstantial.

But I have to say, for this pricing point, this is a nice package to consider including in your bug out bag. You can wear them on your belt, they don't weigh much, and you get three strong blades for the price of one. Just make sure that you also have an excellent folding knife, a sharp and durable fixed blade knife, and a strong tactical tomahawk in your kit. It's always better to have too much of something than nothing at all. And by the way, almost anyone with moderate coordination can learn to throw a knife effectively. Just check out the You-Tube videos and try it out. Lots of fun!
text_fidelity_b: SOG Throwing Knives with Sheath 3 Pack Balanced Throwing Knives Set w/ Paracord Knife Handles and Professional Throwing Knife Sheath (F041TN-CP)

text_fidelity_a:
Nathan Unisex Hydration Back-Pack for Running, Hiking, Cycling and more. 2L Bladder Included / 6L Storage Capacity. Adjustable Straps. NO BOUNCE while Running. I purchased this vest 6 years ago and it served me well in multiple ultras. It has just enough space for everything you need. I just checked the front zip pocket and it's just a tad too small for my Samsung Galaxy S7 Active, which is a thick phone. It definitely wouldn't fit an iPhone 6-7 Plus. The pack rides low enough on your back that there are no real issues with rubbing or chafing of the neck...from the pack. I did get a bit annoyed from time to time by the hose rubbing my neck, though. The side straps....what can I say? Over 6 years, I've never figured out how to adjust them well, lol. But it hasn't seemed to matter much. For a while, I used to over-cinch the chest strap but realized it can stay pretty loose and the pack is still not very bouncy. The front right pocket is where I've always tucked my phone. Although I admit sometimes I've used a SpiBelt with this pack to free up more pocket space for gels. You don't get a whole lot of space in the back pocket but it's perfect for those rarely used but "just in case" items I like to bring like an emergency poncho, extra sunscreen, lip balm, ginger chews, etc.

The bite valve on Nathan's bladder tube has always been problematic for me. I never really "bit" it hard yet within a year or so, it began to leak. After one race, my leg was covered in syrupy goo where gatorade and leaked and evaporated over the course of 50 miles. I swapped it out for the bite valve from a Camelbak and never had another problem. Like all bladders, be religious about cleaning this one post-use or it will gunk up very quickly. The closure system on the bladder takes some getting use to. You'll become a pro at it but for years I watched aid station volunteers stare in bewilderment, trying to figure out how to open it. More often than not, I ended up doing it myself.

I used to find after 100 milers that the top of my back would have a slightly chaffed feel to it, without anything being rubbed raw. I'm sure a light application of body glide or vasoline would have prevented that. But overall, this is a great, basic vest with plenty of fluid capacity. I recently replaced mine with Nathan's VaporAir, mainly for more pockets. But I could easily have bought this again and been happy.
text_fidelity_b: Nathan Unisex Hydration Back-Pack for Running, Hiking, Cycling and more. 2L Bladder Included / 6L Storage Capacity. Adjustable Straps. NO BOUNCE while Running.

text_fidelity_a:
Nordic Walking Poles for Individuals 6’ 2” – 6’ 3” = 132.5cm SWIX of Norway. All 32 Lengths Coming Soon 1-Piece Non-Collapsible. #1 for Hiking, Trekking, Physical Therapy. My review is primarily geared towards people who are interested in learning the Nordic walking techniques and are looking for inexpensive, appropriate walking sticks. It is also a comparison of the sticks offered here and the so-called “crappy Chinese” anti-shock, telescoping sticks. I have purchased both and am including photos below.

I started Nordic walking about 3 or 4 years ago. At the time, I wasn’t sure that this was something I would continue to do and did not want to spend a small fortune on equipment that would, once again, end up unused in a closet. But I was having trouble walking even a short distance (100 ft. or so) without excruciating burning in my legs and back, so thought I needed to give this a shot. I sprang for the cheap sticks and boy, am I glad I did! Within a few weeks, I was walking a mile with very little discomfort. That distance might be laughable to some, but to me, it was a miracle!

But honestly, it had less to do with the type of sticks than it did with learning the proper technique. There are many videos available that demonstrate the technique and anyone interested should spend some time watching them. It is not difficult to learn. In fact once you get the rhythm it’s like riding a bike…you don’t forget how to do it.

As far as the poles go, I see little difference in them. Perhaps at a higher price difference there is, but it’s still more about learning the skills.

Cheap Chinese poles (the black ones in the photos): When I bought mine I made some modifications. The rubber tips that were included wore out quickly. I replaced those with the boot type of tip which has lasted all these years and many miles. The tips are deeply grooved like snow tires and they do pick up small pieces of sand. This will make them slip some on asphalt, but it’s fairly easy to flick a grain of sand out and continue your walk. I also replaced the sponge rubber grip just below the handle (because it tore easily) with some closed cell tubing that I found online. That wasn’t entirely necessary because you never or rarely grab the poles in that area. I should have just eliminated it altogether.

These poles are the twist lock telescoping type (not the clamp type), which is handy when you don’t know what length pole you need in the beginning. But once adjusted, it is a PITA to collapse or readjust them. They do have a scale on them that shows the length you’ve set them to, so if you get these, make a note or find some way of marking the length. I never collapse mine anymore, because I want to start walking immediately, not fiddle with adjustments. However, if you need to pack your walking sticks, and don’t mind messing with the twist locks, this is certainly a consideration when you buy. I have never had the twist locks fail or accidently collapse once snuggly hand tightened.

These poles also have the anti-shock springs. It makes them heavier and, yes, they make a rattling noise every time the pole hits the pavement. Their extra weight does makes their footfall more forceful. I see no advantage to the springs at this point, but I’ve heard that they are helpful when going down steep terrain. Can’t say, because most of my walking is on fairly level pavement. BUT, DO NOT let the noise stop you from buying if you don’t want to spend a lot of money in the beginning. Getting you walking again is far more important than any minor rattles.

The handle grips are very comfortable and include a strap for your hands to go up through. I found these straps were much more comfortable for me and more convenient to use. Just remember to insert your hand up from the bottom of the strap.

Overall, these poles have a bigger diameter than the “real” ones and are slightly heavier. However, I think the few added ounces actually give you a better upper body and arm workout than the lighter poles. So, to me, the extra weight could be advantageous. Cost for these poles was 14.95 for each pole (@29.90). The Leki replacement tips cost $17.31 with tax, and I highly recommend them. I’m not including the rubber grip which is not necessary, so my actual cost was $47.21 with tax.

Real Nordic walking sticks (blue in the photos): As noted above, these are somewhat lighter, thinner, nonadjustable, non-spring-loaded poles. It is important that you order the right length. They adjustable have glove like straps attached to the handle.

Personally, I’m not entirely pleased with these particular straps. As you will see in the photos, their design leaves something to be desired. I have circled the points where they irritate my hands. And here, I will have to make some kind of modification if I want to use these poles for an extended time. The gloves interfere with wearing my fitness watch and the binding on some corners should be more rounded instead of squared off. Strapping your hand in or out, by means of Velcro strips, is awkward; and should you need to let go of your poles if you fall, you’re out of luck. There is a means of length adjustment (by pulling upward on the handle top) which is lacking in the Chinese poles, but it doesn’t solve the rubbing issues, since the part which cradles your hand doesn’t change position. After I have used these poles more, I may try to fashion a strap comparable to the ones on the Chinese poles.

The handles themselves are thinner and (though you shouldn’t be clasping them tightly) may be more suited to smaller hands. I can’t say for sure, but they are still comfortable.

I have a gut feeling that the boot tips on these sticks will wear quickly, needing to be replaced often. However, they do not have the deep tread of the Leki replacement tips and do not pick up grains of rock or sand, so that is an advantage as far as sliding on pavement goes. I will most likely replace these stock tips with the Leki ones and just deal with the rocks.

The cost for these poles (before any changes I may make) is, at this writing, $77.45 including tax and/or shipping. I am, otherwise, perfectly satisfied with these “real” Nordic walking sticks. They are light, not noisy and do what they’re supposed to do.

Both poles need some slight modification, but their functions are identical. Once again, it’s about technique, not one type of pole compared to another. Please do not let any hype make your decision. It’s far more important that you get out there and start walking.
I'm awarding 5 stars to either kind of pole. Both work pretty much equally.
text_fidelity_b: Nordic Walking Poles for Individuals 6’ 2” – 6’ 3” = 132.5cm SWIX of Norway. All 32 Lengths Coming Soon 1-Piece Non-Collapsible. #1 for Hiking, Trekking, Physical Therapy.

text_fidelity_a:
King Koil Twin Air Mattress with Built-in Pump - Double High Elevated Raised Airbed for Guests with Comfortable Top Inflatable Bed with 1-Year Guarantee from The Manufacturer This mattress looked great out of the box. Now less than ten days later it's on its way to the garbage bin.

It looked good at first. The material seemed high-quality and the built-in pump worked great to inflate it, relatively quickly. I went online while the mattress was inflating and read all of the manufacturer's suggestions, including the one to inflate it and let it sit overnight before use to "stretch out", then add more air. I followed all the instructions carefully.

Just a few hours after fully inflating the mattress and without anyone using it or even sitting on it, I pressed on it with my hand and noticed it was already mushy and not nearly as firm as when first inflated, so I topped the air off again and let it sit overnight without using it. The next morning it was mushy again, but I figured maybe this was the "stretching" the manufacturer was talking about. That night I inflated the mattress to full firmness, made up the bed, and went to sleep. About three hours later I woke up with the hard floor under me and a tangle of deflated air mattress wrapped around me.

So clearly, the mattress was defective and had arrived with a leak. Well, that happens. It was really unfortunate because I had no other bed at the time to use, but I had gotten a cheerful email from the manufacturer here on Amazon right after I ordered, telling me if I had any problems to contact them and they would be sure to honor that warranty twhich hey make such a big deal of offering, and make things right.

I emailed them to let them know that right out of the box the mattress was leaking air badly. They replied with the same instructions I found online, saying it was probably "stretching out" and I just needed to top the air off. I replied that I had now spent two nights on the mattress, and the only way to use it was to set an alarm to wake up every two-and-a-half hours to reinflate it before it went completely flat. I asked them to please do as they said and work with me to make it right.

That more than a week and three emails ago. I have emailed them over and over (the only way to reach them.) The manufacturer simply stopped responding after the first email. They did not provide any customer support, no advice, nothing. They did nothing at all to honor the warranty they offer. I tried finding a patch kit on my own for this thing, but I can't even find the leak, it seems to be in the sealing of one of the seams. It's basically garbage at this point, because it's useless. The photo is of it sitting waiting to go out with the trash less than two weeks after being bought.

If you look at the one and two star reviews, many people have had the same issue. With this mattress, it seems like either you are one of the lucky ones and it works perfectly out of the box, or it just doesn't hold air at all and you are screwed, because the manufacturer is not going to keep their word and honor that reassuring-sounding warranty that they offer to entice people into buying their expensive air mattress.

So, if you need a bed and want to roll the dice, try your luck. I did, and I certainly regret believing the untrustworthy, dishonorable shysters who manufacture the King Koil.

$150 dollars, straight out into the trash.

text_fidelity_a:
Men Waders Waterproof Chest Waders Bootfoot Chest Wader Light Hunting Fly Fishing Waders for Men with Boots Nylon/PVC Wader Camouflage/Brown 8-14 Seems like a few fake reviews on these... how 'bout a real one?

I bought these for a week-long trip to Alaska for salmon fishing on the lower Kenai River. My expectation was that I would throw them out at the end of the trip - instead I brought them home. They mostly met my expectations but are not a 5-star product.

Cons:
- The boots fit fine, sure, but the waders were otherwise too small. I'm 6'1, 270 lbs with a 55" beer gut, and have a 33-1/2 inseam. The bottoms went up to my crotch with a little slack, but the top and suspender straps are way too short. I had the buckles on the straps adjusted to the longest length without them constantly coming out (they did occasionally) and the straps really dug in to my shoulders. The straps should be at least six inches longer, but even better the upper part of the waders should be six inches taller. It was a bit of work to get them over my belly but I got to where I could do it over a hoodie and they were snug but not tight. If your inseam is longer than 34" and you're not going to get at least size 13, these won't fit.
- I could stand in them, but crouching or sitting without keeping my legs straight was impossible. There's no stretch in the fabric.
- The top of the pocket on mine is at my navel. Plus, no Velcro or snaps to keep it closed. I got river water inside, and constantly had things falling out. I lost a rented knife I had to replace and my $300 prescription sunglasses to the river.
- The boots don't have a comfortable insole and are really hard. I bought the $15 Dr. Scholls which worked fine.
- When standing in more than a foot of water the boot uppers would collapse and cause considerable pain to the tops of my feet, often to my toes.
- No breathability. My legs and lower trunk got nice and sweaty.

Pros:
+ All the joints are sealed and taped. I didn't have a drop of water on me from the outside.
+ Boots fit well.
+ Construction and materials are good for the price in my subjective opinion.

Neutral:
~ They are unlined. I knew this before buying them. Even wearing jeans my legs got really cold. Plan appropriately.

I wish someone had written a similar review before I bought these and had them arrive. I could have made the needed modifications before I left. With that said, I would not hesitate to buy these again or recommend them to a (very warm-blooded) friend.
text_fidelity_b: Men Waders Waterproof Chest Waders Bootfoot Chest Wader Light Hunting Fly Fishing Waders for Men with Boots Nylon/PVC Wader Camouflage/Brown 8-14

text_fidelity_a: Fishing Hat Sun Protection UPF 50+ Cap with Breathable Mesh Safari Hats for Men Women - Dark Grey This Fishing Hat Sun Hat with Sunscreen and UV Protection is a nice hat and one I’m glad to have. We live in a warm weather state and time at the pool and beach is a must. But that also means exposure to sun both directly and indirectly. I have sensitive skin - and we all need to be careful of sun exposure - so I learned from my dad to wear a hat as often as you can. I gabbed this Fishing Hat Sun Hat with Sunscreen and UV Protection to protect my head and face and so far, it’s working great. I like the color - it’s a black, though not stark, but a bit of a “faded” black. I have another, similar hat that the top stands “taller” than this - I’d describe this one as “streamlined” which is fine. I really like the venting around the head for keeping my head cool, but still protected. There is a “band” that goes around the inside - I think it’s for protecting the forehead from sweat - which is fine - I do not feel it. There is also the ability to tighten the area around the head to make it tighter. I do not need this - I’ve got a pretty big head - but if my wife were to borrow it she might - we have not used this option yet. I’ve worn it in the pool and it worked great. It cannot protect from the reflective light, but it keeps the sun off my head and that’s what I’m looking for - and for that it worked perfectly. I do take the “strap” and tuck in up over the sides and into the tightener strap at the back to keep it out of the way. If you needed it for keeping the hat on, however, it’s there. Overall this is a nice hat and I’m really glad I got it. I will most certainly get a lot of use out of this Fishing Hat Sun Hat with Sunscreen and UV Protection.
text_fidelity_b: Fishing Hat Sun Protection UPF 50+ Cap with Breathable Mesh Safari Hats for Men Women - Dark Grey
